profiles.title: The Meeting of the Lord in the Temple
profiles.subject: Feasts

overview.text: The Meeting of the Lord concerns the forty-day-old Christ brought to Jerusalem and recognized by Simeon and the prophetess Anna. Hopko’s account identifies the feast with the biblical event of Luke 2 and gives February 2 as its calendar date.
overview.reason: A necessary concise account of a copyrighted modern publication; no permission to reproduce its full explanation has been established. This is a labelled AI-written summary, not the source author's wording.

blocks.text: Simeon receives Christ while Mary and Anna stand nearby. Joseph carries the birds offered under the Law; a canopied altar identifies the Temple setting.
blocks.reason: A necessary concise account of a copyrighted modern publication; no permission to reproduce its full explanation has been established. This is a labelled AI-written summary, not the source author's wording.

blocks.text: Led by the Holy Spirit, Simeon recognizes the Messiah and speaks the words now heard at Orthodox Vespers. He also foretells opposition to Christ and sorrow for Mary. Anna thanks God and tells others who await Jerusalem’s redemption. The published explanation places the encounter within the Mosaic Law: the divine Lawgiver is carried as an infant and fulfills the Law he gave.

blocks.text: Hopko explains the feast through this meeting with the incarnate Son, not only through a recollection of the past. He connects Simeon’s words with the Church’s witness to salvation and identifies the light revealed to the Gentiles. The infant received by Simeon and the one worshiped as God are the same Christ.
